questions: Trace durable state under power loss, quota pauses, stale leases and cancellation.
Preserve product files and Plan 2 inputs while deleting only verified control artifacts.
decision: Use owned, generation-aware leases and scoped receipt validity for resume; keep cleanup local, guarded and independent of model judgment.
code_observations: lifecyclectl uses an active pointer and runner lease to prevent duplicate execution, recover interrupted tasks and guard cleanup.
The reusable project resource map is outside disposable plan directories. The former Plan2-input exception is no longer needed, but prepared research is still a retained project artifact.
implementation_steps: Use PID plus process-start identity and host identity when deciding whether a local lease is live. Treat uncertain remote leases conservatively.
Add fault-injection tests around claim, checkpoint, atomic replacement and lease release; ensure recovery never fabricates validation or completion.
Keep cancel/reset scoped to recognized plan roots and registered jobs. Never run an indiscriminate git clean/reset or remove product source/tests.
Pin successful validation receipts to the source/command/map state that produced them; reuse a receipt only if those inputs still match.
Preserve prepared reports outside disposable controls and retain incomplete plan state on failure. Document portable relocation rather than asking users to edit task status manually.
Fence task completion by lease generation and verify process-start identity before process actions.
Represent ambiguous post-crash effects as uncertain and require reconciliation before replay.
Use scoped contract/input fingerprints for task receipts and reserve whole-repository fingerprints for integration checks.
proposed_acceptance_tests: A reused PID does not authorize killing an unrelated process.
Interruptions after each state-write boundary retain completed subtasks and recover only in-progress state.
Symlinks, parent paths and directories without the plan sentinel cannot be cleaned.
Cancelled jobs are stopped before their control directory is removed.
Successful cleanup preserves implementation, tests, shared resource inventory and research reports.
A reused PID cannot satisfy an old lease or be killed by a stale controller.
A runner that lost its lease cannot publish task completion.
An unrelated file change does not invalidate a task receipt while its actual dependency change does.

alternatives.tradeoff: Cheap; PID reuse and stale writers. Reject

cost_model: Saved valid work avoids model redispatch. Count duplicated attempts and recovery reads; correctness takes priority when the prior execution may have produced side effects.
unverified: Power loss, network filesystems and Windows locks require actual platform tests; POSIX mocks are not proof of those guarantees.
Cross-host filesystems, power-loss durability and platform process behavior require dedicated integration tests; a local lease design does not prove distributed exactly-once execution.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Harden crash recovery and cleanup around ownership, process identity and durable receipts; retain the file-backed lifecycle instead of introducing a distributed workflow service.
revision_delta: The revision adds fencing against stale runners, an explicit uncertain-execution outcome and scoped fingerprints; PID existence and whole-repository hash equality are not enough.
decision_analysis: PID reuse can make a dead runner look alive or make a stale controller target a different process. Lease ownership should include host, PID, process start identity and generation. A runner that loses ownership must not complete a task afterward. Remote-host uncertainty should pause with a diagnosable reason instead of killing or launching processes speculatively.

Crash recovery must separate a task that never started, one whose worker exited, and one whose external side effect may have occurred without a saved result. The last state is uncertain, not automatically retryable. Reconcile outputs or use operation-specific idempotency before reexecuting migrations or paid requests.

A valid receipt depends on the tested command, acceptance contract, environment and relevant source/dependency digests. Hashing the whole evolving repository for every task can make legitimate earlier receipts stale after unrelated work. Prefer scoped fingerprints plus a final composed integration run; retain global receipts for genuinely global validation only.

Cleanup removes owned control artifacts after acceptance, not source, live application logs or prepared research. Resolve roots, reject symlinks and require sentinel ownership. Preserve failed-plan evidence. Relocation should use a guarded controller operation or recreation from the specification, not hand editing status fields.

ownership: This implementation owns its declared write scope and acceptance tests. Its following review checks the actual changed code; prepared research is not acceptance evidence.
baseline_anchor_check: All listed file hashes matched the preserved 0.11.0 source in this revision. This is integrity checking, not a second full code audit.
applicability_rule: Refresh only evidence contradicted by the installed CLI, selected account/billing plan or changed code contract. Unknown required capability blocks that candidate; it does not justify widening permissions.
